chapter_summaries: The narrator introduces Fyodor Pavlovitch Karamazov, a senseless, vicious, buffoonish landowner who rose from nothing to a fortune of a hundred thousand roubles. Married twice, he had three sons: Dmitri by his first wife Adelaïda Ivanovna, and Ivan and Alexey by his second. Adelaïda, a wealthy noblewoman of the Miüsov family, eloped with him, quickly came to despise him, and finally ran away with a divinity student to Petersburg, leaving the three-year-old Dmitri behind. When news came of her death, Fyodor reacted with both drunken joy and weeping.
events: Fyodor Pavlovitch rises from next to nothing to amass a hundred thousand roubles by his death.
Fyodor Pavlovitch and Adelaïda Ivanovna elope and marry, though without mutual love.
Fyodor seizes Adelaïda's money (up to twenty-five thousand roubles) and tries to transfer her property to his name, but her family intervenes.
Adelaïda runs away with a divinity student to Petersburg, leaving the three-year-old Mitya with Fyodor.
Fyodor turns the house into a harem of drunken orgies and tours the province parading himself as the injured husband.
News arrives of Adelaïda's sudden death in Petersburg; the drunken Fyodor reacts with both shouts of joy and uncontrolled weeping.
